title: Normalized root-tower boundary comparison and naturality diagrams
statement: Let p be a natural number, R a commutative ring and t:Fin r -> R. Use the existing compatible-root algebra [def-sfb-strict-local-kummer-tame-module], full projection and product-inverting open [lem-sfb-root-tower-lisse-morphism-extension]. Set S=Spec(R/(t_i)); evaluation setting every compatible root to zero kills the defining relations, hence defines i:S->T over the closed inclusion s:S->Spec R. Its defining square and its actual profinite-test squares commute. All test maps, exact pullback identifications and exchange arrows are those of [lem-sfb-root-tower-coordinate-face]. For a normed field F, use the coefficients and canonical derived evaluation beta of [def-sfb-derived-profinite-evaluation], and an internal module N on T with a supplied identification e:i^*N isomorphic to p_S^*B, form the full source s^*Rq_{P,*}N_P[0], open source s^*Rv_{P,*}j_P^*N_P[0], target p_S^*R internalHom(C_F[P],B[0]), and the actual map lambda from full source to open source induced by N_P->Rj_{P,*}j_P^*N_P. Define fullRestriction by the actual boundary exchange adjunct followed by the pullback of e. A NormalizedComparison means lambda and beta_{S,P}(B[0]) are isomorphisms and there exists an isomorphism alpha from open source to target with lambda alpha beta=fullRestriction. Normalization is that displayed equation for a specified alpha. Define the commutative squares for module and boundary-model morphisms, continuous parameter maps, and pro-etale base changes with commuting full, open and boundary test squares; the last uses the entire supplied full-tower module arrow, induces its open and boundary arrows by pullback, and uses the actual exchange and evaluation arrows on both sides. It therefore includes profinite families as equations on whole parametrized test schemes, not just their points. Assertion F p t E is this normalized comparison for every finite-dimensional E-space M, every supplied lisse N [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module] and boundary identification with M_F, together with the three naturality diagrams. The empty-coordinate, empty-parameter, zero-module and empty-stratum cases are included.
